name: New Zealand
summary: There is no fixed share for children, but the Family Protection Act 1955 lets a court award a share to a spouse, partner, children and others, and the Property (Relationships) Act 1976 gives a surviving partner a choice between a relationship-property split and the will. New Zealand has its own Trusts Act 2019 but has not joined the Hague Trusts Convention. There is no private foundation.
family_claims: Family Protection Act 1955 (claims by spouse/partner, children, step-children, grandchildren, parents in limited cases); Law Reform (Testamentary Promises) Act 1949; Property (Relationships) Act 1976 Part 8 (surviving partner's option to take a property split instead of the will).
foreign_law_note: Succession to movables follows the deceased's last domicile and succession to land follows the law of its location (common-law conflict rules); there is no choice of law by nationality. Family Protection Act claims can apply to NZ-domiciled estates and to NZ land.
trust_note: Trusts Act 2019 (in force 30 Jan 2021) codifies trust law; trusts can be foreign or domestic. NZ does not appear on the HCCH Convention table. Foreign trusts are recognised under common law rules. Foreign-sourced-income trusts have a special trust regime (non-resident trustee, foreign trust disclosure rules). No private foundation statute exists; charitable boards are incorporated under the Charitable Trusts Act 1957.
open_questions: Confirm Family Protection Act 1955 reach over estates of foreign domiciliaries with NZ assets.
Confirm that no Hague Trusts Convention accession is pending.
